policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'But his neighbor cometh and searcheth him out' renders the verb with a bare English present that fits either the qere waw-consecutive perfect (ובא) or the ketiv imperfect (יבא) in this gnomic proverb; both readings carry the same lexeme בוא and the same subject, and no ASV note is mapped to this unit, so the English distinguishes nothing.

ASV 'And such contentions are like the bars of a castle' renders a plural noun of strife that answers equally to the qere מדינים and the ketiv מדונים, alternate plural spellings of the same word; the only note on the verse is classed alternative_rendering ('Or, injured') and bears on the participle earlier in the line, not on this unit.
